parsed.why: Authorities actively pursue people perceived as gay or gender-nonconforming; trans women face documented assault, detention and flogging under a regime permitting death for same-sex activity. State-directed persecution and escalating moral enforcement make discovery catastrophic.

No trans-specific criminalisation or documented visitor-facing restrictions; social and institutional signals are comparatively welcoming, though mostly LGB-focused. A trans activist reported verbal abuse and two attacks, and no reliable trans-specific acceptance or protection evidence fills the gaps.

A newly passed, not-yet-assented bill would criminalise identifying as trans and impose a duty to report, amid existing same-sex criminalisation, mob justice and documented hostility. Pending status reduces certainty, but the operative climate remains seriously threatening.

Authorities use a criminal provision to arrest people for gender expression; police humiliation, forced exposure allegations and public outing are documented. Recent trans-specific reporting describes systemic hostility, while arrests and weak protection make institutional recourse unreliable.

The 2024 ruling exempts private consensual adult conduct, and no trans-specific targeting or visitor restriction is documented. But past arrests, violence, dismissive police responses and hostility toward gay tourists signal residual risk; the trans-specific evidence is notably sparse.
